reference_sql:
SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', order_ts) AS DATE) AS order_month,
       COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', order_ts)
alternatives: SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', order_ts) AS DATE) AS order_month, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY 1
SELECT make_date(year(order_ts), month(order_ts), 1) AS order_month, COUNT(order_id) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY year(order_ts), month(order_ts)

other_way.sql: SELECT make_date(year(order_ts), month(order_ts), 1) AS order_month, COUNT(order_id) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY year(order_ts), month(order_ts)
other_way.tradeoff: Building the date from the year and the month gives the same months, but date_trunc does it in one call.
